## 2. Deep Dive: Apache Kafka Internals - The Commit Log

URL: https://yashasav.dev/posts/apache-kafka-internals-commit-log/

Kafka is fundamentally an append-only, immutable commit log persisted on disk, divided into partitions and segments.
Key concepts covered:
- **Sequential Disk I/O**: Kafka bypasses random disk access by appending records sequentially, achieving throughput comparable to network speeds.
- **Page Cache & Zero-Copy (`sendfile`)**: Operating system page cache handles reads/writes. Transfer from page cache to socket bypasses user-space buffer copies via Linux `sendfile` syscall.
- **Segment Files & Sparse Indexes**: Topics are divided into partitions; partitions are split into segment files (`.log`). Offset indexes (`.index`) and timestamp indexes (`.timeindex`) enable O(log N) binary search for record retrieval.
- **Consumer Lag & Backpressure**: Consumers pull data at their own pace based on current committed offsets vs log end offset (LEO). Backpressure is consumer-driven rather than broker-push.

---

## 3. Deep Dive: PagedAttention vs RadixAttention

URL: https://yashasav.dev/posts/paged-attention-vs-radix-attention/

Memory management in LLM serving runtimes determines throughput and token generation efficiency.
Key concepts covered:
- **PagedAttention (vLLM)**: Solves external and internal memory fragmentation in Key-Value (KV) caching by dynamic virtual memory paging. Allocates non-contiguous block tables for KV cache tensors.
- **RadixAttention (SGLang)**: Solves prefix reuse across multiple requests by maintaining KV cache blocks in a Radix Tree (trie) data structure. Allows rapid matching, automatic LRU eviction, and sub-tree sharing for system prompts, few-shot examples, and agent tool call loops.

## 4. Research Publication: BloBS-FL

Title: BloBS-FL: A Robust Architecture of Blockchain Based Decentralized Split Federated Learning
Publication: IEEE / COMSNETS 2026
URL: https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/11418208/

Overview:
Presents a robust decentralized architecture combining split federated learning with blockchain ledgers to eliminate single points of failure, prevent malicious gradient manipulation, and preserve data privacy in edge device model training.
